messages.subject: geomorph data frame creation
parts:
Hello, 

I was wondering if you could clarify something about the geomorph data frames for me. I recently tried running some code that I wrote a while back and started to receive an error about name matching when running the procD.pgls() function. The only way I managed to solve the error was by importing data straight into the geomorph data frame without reordering the species in my dataset and shape data to match the order of the phy file.
If I do not do this,  I receive all TRUE if checking names using %in% but mostly FALSE if using == (e.g., rownames(Metadata) %in% Tree$tip.label returns TRUE but  rownames(Metadata) == Tree$tip.label doesn't).
I just wanted to make sure that all the data will be attributed to correct species when assessing the geomorph data frame if I don't match the order of the species names before import?
Sorry if I have missed this being asked before.
Thank you!

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] geomorph data frame creation
parts:
Dear Phoebe,

The procD.pgls function requires matching of tree tip names and rownames/names of data and will sort a covariance matrix to match the order of observations based on the matched names.  Although I cannot guess why an error was alleviated by using a geomorph data frame, I can attest that using a geomorph data frame alleviates many possible errors.  Using a data frame precisely describes the environment in which the analysis is performed.  It means the function does not have to search for a variable or data in the global environment and try to make sense of it.  

Best,
mike
